skills.summary: Stops an agent dropping a database it should never have been pointed at.
skills.signature: 18 destructive command shapes, stopped before they run
skills.description: Block destructive database commands before they run: DROP, TRUNCATE, unqualified DELETE or UPDATE, and resets like supabase db reset, whenever they are aimed at anything that is not clearly a local development database. Runs as a PreToolUse hook. Local only - no network.
highlights: Runs as a PreToolUse hook, so a destructive command is stopped rather than reported
Blocks DROP, TRUNCATE and WHERE-less DELETE or UPDATE against anything not clearly local
Asks instead of blocking when the target is a local database, because resetting dev is normal work
Treats a connection it cannot read as production - $DATABASE_URL is not a safe assumption
skills.requires: python3 (already on macOS and Linux). Claude Code, for the hook. No network.
skills.notes: It reads the command, not the database. SQL inside a file passed with psql -f is invisible to it, as is anything that does not go through Bash. It is a speed bump on an irreversible action, not a backup.

skills.name: db-guard
skills.description: Block destructive database commands before they run - DROP, TRUNCATE, unqualified DELETE or UPDATE, and resets like supabase db reset or prisma migrate reset - whenever they are aimed at anything that is not clearly a local development database. Use when the user asks to protect their database, mentions dropping or truncating tables, resetting or wiping a database, running a migration against production, is worried an agent will delete their data, or asks what db-guard blocked and why.

skills.summary: Find the access-control holes that get shipped apps breached, before you ship.
skills.signature: 10 rule codes, file and line on every finding
skills.description: Audit a Supabase or Postgres app for access-control holes before it ships: tables with row level security off, policies that let everyone through, service role keys reachable from the browser, and paywalls enforced only in client code. Local files only - no network.
highlights: Every table in the public schema without row level security, named and located
Policies that are technically on but let everyone through - using (true), with check (true)
Service role keys sitting anywhere the browser can read them, including client components
Separates what is proven from what is pattern-matched, and never fails a build on a guess
skills.requires: python3 (already on macOS and Linux). Reads your project files only. No network.
skills.notes: Static analysis of migration files and source. Tables created through the Supabase dashboard rather than a migration are invisible to it, and a clean result is not a guarantee - the report says so itself.

skills.name: rls-audit
skills.description: Audit a Supabase or Postgres app for access-control holes before it ships - tables with row level security switched off, policies that let everyone through, service role keys reachable from the browser, and paywalls enforced only in client code. Use when the user asks whether their app is safe to launch, mentions RLS, row level security, Supabase policies, a security or pre-launch audit, a leaked or exposed API key, whether their paywall or auth can be bypassed, or says they are about to deploy or go live.

skills.summary: Find the credentials you are leaking, and the ones git remembers even after you deleted them.
skills.signature: 16 credential types, and it reads git history
skills.description: Find credentials your project is leaking: API keys written into source, secrets in browser-exposed variables, env files tracked by git or sitting in its history, and keys baked into Dockerfiles or CI workflows. Never prints a secret in full. Local files only - no network.
highlights: Sixteen provider signatures, from Stripe and AWS to Supabase service_role keys
Reads git history, so an env file you deleted last month is still reported
Never prints a secret in full - the report does not become another copy of the key
Stays quiet about keys in a properly ignored .env, because that is where they belong
skills.requires: python3 (already on macOS and Linux). Reads your project files and runs git log. No network.
skills.notes: Finds what is on disk and in git history. It cannot tell you whether a leaked key has already been used - that needs the provider's logs - and it cannot see secrets already set in a deployed environment.

skills.name: secret-sweep
skills.description: Find credentials your project is leaking - API keys and tokens written into source, secrets in browser-exposed variables, env files tracked by git or sitting in its history, and keys baked into Dockerfiles or CI workflows. Use when the user asks whether they have leaked a key, mentions exposed or committed secrets, .env in git, a compromised or rotated API key, an unexpected bill on an API account, or wants a pre-launch check before making a repository public or shipping.

skills.summary: What an order actually earns once GST, shipping, payment fees and COD returns are taken out.
skills.signature: CM1 to CM3, max CAC, breakeven ROAS, discount floor
skills.description: Work out what a D2C order actually earns after GST, product cost, packing, shipping, payment fees, COD returns and marketing: CM1/CM2/CM3, max CAC, breakeven ROAS and the discount floor.
highlights: CM1, CM2 and CM3 per order, with GST stripped out of revenue where it belongs
Models COD and prepaid separately, then blends them - including what RTO costs you
Gives you the most you can pay per order, the breakeven ROAS, and the discount floor

skills.notes: Estimates from the numbers you supply, not accounts. GST input credit on costs is not modelled, and returns are treated as stock recovered with freight lost.
